15.text: “Let it be so now,” Jesus replied. “It is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness in this way.” Then John permitted Him.

4.text: But Jesus answered, “It is written: ‘Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.’ ”

7.text: Jesus replied, “It is also written: ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’ ”

10.text: “Away from Me, Satan!” Jesus told him. “For it is written: ‘Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only.’ ”

17.text: From that time on Jesus began to preach, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near.” The First Disciples ( Mark 1:16–20|MRK 1:16-20; Luke 5:1–11|LUK 5:1-11; John 1:35–42|JHN 1:35-42 )

19.text: “Come, follow Me,” Jesus said, “and I will make you fishers of men.”

3.text: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

4.text: Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.

5.text: Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.

6.text: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled.

7.text: Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.

8.text: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.

9.text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called sons of God.

10.text: Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

11.text: Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of Me.

12.text: Rejoice and be glad, because great is your reward in heaven, for in the same way they persecuted the prophets before you. Salt and Light ( Mark 9:49–50|MRK 9:49-50; Luke 14:34–35|LUK 14:34-35; Philippians 2:12–18|PHP 2:12-18 )

13.text: You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt loses its savor, how can it be made salty again? It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled by men.

14.text: You are the light of the world. A city on a hill cannot be hidden.

15.text: Neither do people light a lamp and put it under a basket. Instead, they set it on a stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house.

16.text: In the same way, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven. The Fulfillment of the Law

17.text: Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I have not come to abolish them, but to fulfill them.

18.text: For I tell you truly, until heaven and earth pass away, not a single jot, not a stroke of a pen, will disappear from the Law until everything is accomplished.

19.text: So then, whoever breaks one of the least of these commandments and teaches others to do likewise will be called least in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever practices and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.

20.text: For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven. Anger and Reconciliation ( Luke 12:57–59|LUK 12:57-59 )

21.text: You have heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘Do not murder’ and ‘Anyone who murders will be subject to judgment.’

22.text: But I tell you that anyone who is angry with his brother will be subject to judgment. Again, anyone who says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ will be subject to the Sanhedrin. But anyone who says, ‘You fool!’ will be subject to the fire of hell.

23.text: So if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you,

24.text: leave your gift there before the altar. First go and be reconciled to your brother; then come and offer your gift.

25.text: Reconcile quickly with your adversary, while you are still on the way to court. Otherwise, he may hand you over to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the officer, and you may be thrown into prison.

26.text: Truly I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the last penny. Adultery ( Leviticus 18:1–30|LEV 18:1-30 )

27.text: You have heard that it was said, ‘Do not commit adultery.’

28.text: But I tell you that anyone who looks at a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.

29.text: If your right eye causes you to sin, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to be thrown into hell.

30.text: And if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to depart into hell. Divorce ( Deuteronomy 24:1–5|DEU 24:1-5; Luke 16:18|LUK 16:18 )

31.text: It has also been said, ‘Whoever divorces his wife must give her a certificate of divorce.’

32.text: But I tell you that anyone who divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, brings adultery upon her. And he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery. Oaths and Vows ( Numbers 30:1–16|NUM 30:1-16 )

33.text: Again, you have heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘Do not break your oath, but fulfill your vows to the Lord.’

34.text: But I tell you not to swear at all: either by heaven, for it is God’s throne;

35.text: or by the earth, for it is His footstool; or by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.

36.text: Nor should you swear by your head, for you cannot make a single hair white or black.

37.text: Simply let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes,’ and your ‘No,’ ‘No.’ Anything more comes from the evil one. Love Your Enemies ( Leviticus 24:17–23|LEV 24:17-23; Luke 6:27–36|LUK 6:27-36 )

38.text: You have heard that it was said, ‘Eye for eye and tooth for tooth.’

39.text: But I tell you not to resist an evil person. If someone slaps you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also;

40.text: if someone wants to sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well;

41.text: and if someone forces you to go one mile, go with him two miles.

42.text: Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you.

43.text: You have heard that it was said, ‘Love your neighbor’ and ‘Hate your enemy.’

44.text: But I tell you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,

45.text: that you may be sons of your Father in heaven. He causes His sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.

46.text: If you love those who love you, what reward will you get? Do not even tax collectors do the same?

47.text: And if you greet only your brothers, what are you doing more than others? Do not even Gentiles do the same?

48.text: Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.’’

1.text: “ Be careful not to perform your righteous acts before men to be seen by them. If you do, you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.

2.text: So when you give to the needy, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and on the streets, to be honored by men. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.

3.text: But when you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,

4.text: so that your giving may be in secret. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you. The Lord’s Prayer ( Luke 11:1–4|LUK 11:1-4 )

5.text: And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites. For they love to pray standing in the synagogues and on the street corners to be seen by men. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.

6.text: But when you pray, go into your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.

7.text: And when you pray, do not babble on like pagans, for they think that by their many words they will be heard.

8.text: Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.

9.text: So then, this is how you should pray: ‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name.

10.text: Your kingdom come, Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.

11.text: Give us this day our daily bread.

12.text: And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.

13.text: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. ’

14.text: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.

15.text: But if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive yours. Proper Fasting

16.text: When you fast, do not be somber like the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces to show men they are fasting. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.

17.text: But when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,

18.text: so that your fasting will not be obvious to men, but only to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you. Treasures in Heaven ( Luke 12:32–34|LUK 12:32-34 )

19.text: Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.

20.text: But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where moth and rust do not destroy, and where thieves do not break in and steal.

21.text: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also. The Lamp of the Body ( Luke 11:33–36|LUK 11:33-36 )

22.text: The eye is the lamp of the body. If your eyes are good, your whole body will be full of light.

23.text: But if your eyes are bad, your whole body will be full of darkness. If then the light within you is darkness, how great is that darkness!

24.text: No one can serve two masters: Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money. Do Not Worry ( Luke 12:22–31|LUK 12:22-31 )

25.text: Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothes?

26.text: Look at the birds of the air: They do not sow or reap or gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more valuable than they?

27.text: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?

28.text: And why do you worry about clothes? Consider how the lilies of the field grow: They do not labor or spin.

29.text: Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.

30.text: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, will He not much more clothe you, O you of little faith?

31.text: Therefore do not worry, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’

32.text: For the Gentiles strive after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them.

33.text: But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added unto you.

34.text: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Today has enough trouble of its own.’’

1.text: “Do not judge, or you will be judged.

2.text: For with the same judgment you pronounce, you will be judged, and with the measure you use, it will be measured to you.

3.text: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?

4.text: How can you say to your brother, ‘Let me take the speck out of your eye,’ while there is still a beam in your own eye?

5.text: You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.

6.text: Do not give dogs what is holy; do not throw your pearls before swine. If you do, they may trample them under their feet, and then turn and tear you to pieces. Ask, Seek, Knock ( Luke 11:5–13|LUK 11:5-13 )

7.text: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.

8.text: For everyone who asks receives; he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened.

9.text: Which of you, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone?

10.text: Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a snake?

11.text: So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him!

12.text: In everything, then, do to others as you would have them do to you. For this is the essence of the Law and the Prophets. The Narrow Gate ( Luke 13:22–30|LUK 13:22-30 )

13.text: Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many enter through it.

14.text: But small is the gate and narrow the way that leads to life, and only a few find it. A Tree and Its Fruit ( Luke 6:43–45|LUK 6:43-45 )

15.text: Beware of false prophets. They come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves.

16.text: By their fruit you will recognize them. Are grapes gathered from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?

17.text: Likewise, every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit.

18.text: A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot bear good fruit.

19.text: Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.

20.text: So then, by their fruit you will recognize them.

21.text: Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only he who does the will of My Father in heaven.

22.text: Many will say to Me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Your name, and in Your name drive out demons and perform many miracles?’

23.text: Then I will tell them plainly, ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you workers of lawlessness!’ The House on the Rock ( Luke 6:46–49|LUK 6:46-49 )

24.text: Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on the rock.

25.text: The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house; yet it did not fall, because its foundation was on the rock.

26.text: But everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not act on them is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.

27.text: The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell— and great was its collapse!” The Authority of Jesus

3.text: Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. “I am willing,” He said. “Be clean!” And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.

4.text: Then Jesus instructed him, “See that you don’t tell anyone. But go, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift prescribed by Moses, as a testimony to them.” The Faith of the Centurion ( Luke 7:1–10|LUK 7:1-10; John 4:43–54|JHN 4:43-54 )

7.text: “I will go and heal him,” Jesus replied.

10.text: When Jesus heard this, He marveled and said to those following Him, “Truly I tell you, I have not found anyone in Israel with such great faith.

11.text: I say to you that many will come from the east and the west to share the banquet with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.

12.text: But the sons of the kingdom will be thrown into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”

13.text: Then Jesus said to the centurion, “Go! As you have believed, so will it be done for you.” And his servant was healed at that very hour. Jesus Heals at Peter’s House ( Mark 1:29–34|MRK 1:29-34; Luke 4:38–41|LUK 4:38-41 )

20.text: Jesus replied, “Foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.”

22.text: But Jesus told him, “Follow Me, and let the dead bury their own dead.” Jesus Calms the Storm ( Psalm 107:1–43|PSA 107:1-43; Mark 4:35–41|MRK 4:35-41; Luke 8:22–25|LUK 8:22-25 )

26.text: “ You of little faith,” Jesus replied, “why are you so afraid?” Then He got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and it was perfectly calm.

32.text: “Go!” He told them. So they came out and went into the pigs, and the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea and died in the waters.
